rows.description: Cervical Radiculopathy Involving the C1 Nerve Root (Very Rare)
rows.intro: Due to the unique anatomical position and function of the C1 nerve root, radiculopathy is extremely rare. When affected, it often overlaps with upper cervical or occipital conditions.

CH.lead: (residual symptoms) with mechanism of injury consistent with DX;

PE.lead: confirms residual radicular symptoms of pain or subjectively altered sensory perception (paresthesia-like often described as numbness) without objectively verifiable sensory loss for dullness to pinprick or loss of sharp vs dull perception in a neuroanatomically plausible dermatomal distribution compatible with the C1 dermatome (ie, occipital or upper neck region, radiating from the back of the head toward the crown or forehead, with no significant limb symptoms);

items.text: MRI or CT imaging demonstrating a C1 nerve root injury or lesion

electrodiagnostic findings confirming C1 nerve root pathology consistent with *Guides* CS definitions per Section 17.06e1 Electrodiagnosis of Radiculopathy. Although this test can assist in supporting the diagnosis, it is rarely performed and often fails to provide definitive confirmation. The primary reason lies in the technical challenges involved, as the nerve root primarily innervates muscles in the neck region and, unlike lower cervical nerve roots, lacks representation in limb muscles.
surgeon's clear objective verification of an intraoperative lesion involving the C1 nerve root

items.text: MRI or CT imaging demonstrating a C4 nerve root injury or lesion

electrodiagnostic findings confirming C4 nerve root pathology consistent with *Guides* CS definitions per Section 17.06e1 Electrodiagnosis of Radiculopathy. Although this test can assist in supporting the diagnosis, it is rarely performed and often fails to provide definitive confirmation. The primary reason lies in the technical challenges involved, as the nerve root primarily innervates muscles in the neck region and, unlike lower cervical nerve roots, lacks representation in limb muscles. If the testing meets AANEM criteria for a C5 or C6 radiculopathy, but imaging shows C4 nerve root compression, there is likely a "Pre-Fixed brachial plexus" and this should be rated as if a C5 radiculopathy was present.

rows.description: Cervical Spinal Fracture C1 or C2
rows.intro: Fractures may occur at single or multiple levels. The single fracture with the highest whole person impairment rating is used to calculate impairment.
rows.notes: Unlike those of C3 through C7, common fracture patterns for C1 and C2 do not involve loss of vertebral body height. There is rarely neurologic deficit, as there are no motor branches of significance from C1 and C2 roots. The sensory branches/roots are usually uninjured, or there is so much overlap of sensory innervation the deficit is undetectable. There is no confirmatory electrodiagnostic test for the C1 or C2 roots.

CH.lead: (residual symptoms) with mechanism of injury consistent with DX;

CS.lead: (one of the following) imaging or findings at surgery consistent with DX of

items.text: healed odontoid process fracture
nondisplaced lamina, pedicle or articular process (posterior elements) fracture without loss of structural integrity
displaced spinous process (SP) or transverse process (TP) (posterior elements) fracture without loss of structural integrity

CH.lead: (residual symptoms) with mechanism of injury consistent with DX;

CS.lead: imaging or findings at surgery consistent with DX of posterior element fracture (lamina, pedicle, articular process, spinous process, or transverse process) without dislocation that has healed with or without surgery, often result in range of motion loss. A common complaint after these injuries is difficulty driving due to limited right and left cervical rotation.

CH.lead: (residual symptoms) with mechanism of injury consistent with DX;

CS.lead: imaging or findings at surgery consistent with DX of a posterior element fracture, posterior arch of C1 and pars or pedicle of C2 with displacement disrupting the spinal canal and fracture has healed with or without surgery.

rows.description: Cervical Spinal Fracture C3 to C7
rows.intro: Fractures may occur at single or multiple levels. The single fracture with the highest whole person impairment rating is used to calculate impairment.

CH.lead: (residual symptoms) with mechanism of injury consistent with DX;

nondisplaced lamina, pedicle or articular process (posterior elements) fracture without loss of structural integrity
displaced spinous process (SP) or transverse process (TP) (posterior elements) fracture without loss of structural integrity

rows.description: Cervical AOMSI Associated With Fusion, Arthroplasty, or Pseudarthrosis
rows.notes: The calculated impairment values take into account the potential future stress on the disc spaces adjacent to the surgical site, a condition known as adjacent disc disease or adjacent segment degeneration. This consideration reflects the understanding that the redistribution of mechanical forces following a spinal procedure can accelerate wear and tear on neighboring vertebral levels, potentially leading to additional spinal issues in the future.
